```{r setup}
library(knbsdata)
```

This page states plainly what this release can and cannot do, and why. It is
worth reading before relying on the package for anything that matters.

## Registered sources

```{r}
knbs_sources()
```

```{r}
knbs_status()
```

`knbs_status(live = TRUE)` contacts the verified sources. It never contacts a
source at stability `discovery`, because those have placeholder endpoints and
there is nothing to call.

## What each stability level means

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `discovery` | The endpoint has not been verified. Unusable, and never contacted. |
| `experimental` | Verified and tested, but not documented by its publisher, so it could change without notice. |
| `beta` | Verified, documented and monitored over time. |
| `stable` | A schema contract the package expects to keep. |
| `deprecated` | Scheduled for removal. |

Nothing in this release is above `experimental`.

## What works

**The survey catalogue**, via the Kenya National Data Archive:
`knbs_search_surveys()`, `knbs_survey_metadata()`, `knbs_variables()` and
`knbs_survey_files()`. The archive exposes a JSON API that needs no credentials
for metadata. 129 studies covering 1969–2022 were catalogued at the time of the
audit.

**Publications**, via the KNBS website's media library:
`knbs_publications()` and `knbs_download_publication()`. The site's WordPress
REST API lists roughly 1,600 documents — statistical releases, survey reports,
Economic Survey chapters and workbooks — with direct, ungated file URLs.
Downloads are verified, checksummed and given a provenance sidecar.

Two properties of this source to keep in mind:

- `release_date` is the date a file reached the website, not the publication's
  reference period. The `year` column is read from the title, and is `NA` when
  the title names none.
- The media library also holds speeches, launch remarks and forms. What counts
  as a publication is your `query`, not a curated list.

**Census tables**, via the KNBS census data service (`data.knbs.or.ke`):
`knbs_indicators()` and `knbs_get_indicator()`. Thirty-two tables from the
2019 Population and Housing Census as JSON-stat, under an explicit CC BY 4.0
statement, with geography down to sub-county and leading zeros intact. See
`vignette("census-indicators")`.

One property of this source to keep in mind: **its API host is HTTP-only** —
no TLS listener exists — so traffic to it is unencrypted in transit. It
carries public census aggregates and no credentials, and the registry records
the exception explicitly rather than hiding it.

**Consumer prices**, via the KNBS CPI Explorer (`cpiexplorer.knbs.or.ke`):
`knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS")`, `"CPI_INFLATION_YOY"` and
`"CPI_INFLATION_MOM"` — monthly from January 2009, nationally and by the CPI
collection strata (the Nairobi income bands, Nairobi Combined, Rest of
Urban) — plus `knbs_retail_prices()`, the monthly national average retail
prices of the 22 CPI basket commodities. See
`vignette("census-indicators")`.

Three properties of this source to keep in mind, all carried in
`knbs_metadata()` on every result:

- **The portal states no licence**, unlike the census service's CC BY 4.0
  footer, and does not state the index base period.
- **Its regions are collection strata, not census territories.** Their codes
  must never be joined against `knbs_geographies()`.
- **Six listed regions — the former provinces — carry no data in any
  period.** Asking for them returns zero rows, because that is the source's
  answer.

## What does not, and why

### Microdata cannot be downloaded

The archive requires an account for every download. `knbs_download_microdata()`
explains the official access process and stops. The package does not automate
sign-in, licence acceptance or approval workflows.

This is worth understanding rather than working around: `access_type` of
`public_use` describes the archive's *terms* — public-use files exist — not
whether a program may fetch them.

### Documentation files are not listed

Questionnaires, reports and technical documents have no machine-readable
listing at the archive. Reaching them would mean parsing a web page, which this
package does not do. The `catalogue_url` column from `knbs_search_surveys()`
opens the study on the archive's own site, where they are linked.

### GDP, trade and other running series are still documents

`knbs_get_indicator()` serves census tables and the CPI family. National
accounts, trade and the other recurring series have no verified
machine-readable source, so their monthly and quarterly releases remain
available as documents through `knbs_publications()`.

### Geography: one vintage, no boundaries, no classifications

`knbs_geographies()` serves the 2019 census frame — Kenya, 47 counties,
sub-counties, with names and parent codes, read from the census service's own
Territory dimension. What it does not serve, because nothing has been
verified: other vintages, crosswalks between coding systems, boundary
geometries (`knbs_boundaries()` does not exist) and statistical
classifications. `knbs_search()` across sources also does not exist yet.

### Variable documentation is uneven

Some studies are catalogued with no variable metadata at all, including the most
recent one at the time of the audit. `knbs_variables()` returns zero rows for
those. That is the archive's answer, not a failure.

## How you will know if something changes

The package checks the *shape* of every response, not just its status code.
The archive answers unknown paths with `200` and a study record rather than a
404, so a renamed endpoint would otherwise deliver the wrong object convincingly.
When a payload lacks the fields its operation requires, you get
`knbs_error_schema_changed` and a note that the endpoint has probably moved.

A scheduled job runs `knbs_status(live = TRUE)` weekly against the verified
sources.

## Reporting a change

If a source has moved, changed shape or changed its access rules, please open a
[data source change issue](https://github.com/Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata/issues/new/choose).
Public URLs only — never session-bound URLs, tokens or cookies.

## Disclaimer

`knbsdata` is an independent open-source project. It is not an official KNBS
product unless and until KNBS formally adopts or endorses it. Consult the
original KNBS source for authoritative definitions, revisions, access conditions
and official releases.
